agents.note: SPRINT 66 (V0.29.20) -- US-495 (S2 overlay [hidden] guard + /opt force-refresh) DONE, 2/7. BOTH HALVES OF THIS STORY ARE THE SAME BUG WEARING DIFFERENT CLOTHES: something was only ever ADDED and never SUBTRACTED, so a retired thing kept winning. (1) CSS. Atlas's root cause confirmed, plus ONE MORE offender than the five he listed -- #dtc-ribbon is a sixth and the nastiest, because it also runs `animation: ribbon-pulse 2s infinite`, so an unhidden ribbon pulses a PHANTOM ALERT BAND across every card at idle. That is an F-6 no-phantom violation, not mere clutter. Fix is the global `[hidden] { display: none !important; }`. THE !IMPORTANT IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT DEFENSIVE: an ID selector already outranks any plain [hidden] rule we could write, so the guard must win on IMPORTANCE or be duplicated onto every element -- and the next overlay added would ship the bug again. Consequence documented in the CSS: an element needing present-but-invisible must NOT use `hidden` (aria-hidden + visibility). No JS touched -- Iris's JS was correct throughout and uses el.hidden exclusively (18 call sites, grep-verified). THE TEST IS THE CARRY-FORWARD. I did NOT grep the stylesheet for the guard string. test_dashboard_overlay_hidden_guard.py enumerates every element the SHIPPED MARKUP carries `hidden` on, then resolves the winning `display` through a miniature cascade (importance -> specificity -> source order, real compound-selector matcher). Data-driven from the artifact, so a future overlay is covered the day it is added and the guard cannot be quietly deleted. Went RED naming all six offenders AND their exact winning selectors. Stated fidelity limit for US-499/S6: only compound simple selectors match; a skipped rule makes it LENIENT (falsely green), never falsely red. Also pinned the INVERSE -- each overlay still declares display:flex when NOT hidden -- because the cheap way to pass the guard test is to delete `display: flex`, which would break every overlay's layout while going green. WHEN YOU ADD A GUARD, PIN WHAT THE GUARD MUST NOT COST. (2) STALE /opt. DIAGNOSED BEFORE FIXING, and the diagnosis is the useful part: 'ODB2' appears NOWHERE in this repo (repo-wide grep, zero hits), so the Pi was serving a file from a generation that no longer exists in source. Mechanism: both asset steps only ever installed ON TOP of /opt and NOTHING was ever pruned, and eclipse-states-http searches --assets-dir /opt/splash BEFORE /opt/dashboard -- so one forgotten file in /opt/splash SHADOWS the real asset in /opt/dashboard forever, and the dashboard step (which only writes /opt/dashboard) can never dislodge it. `install -m 0644` overwriting was never the problem; the ABSENCE OF DELETION was. Generalisable: a search path plus an append-only installer is a permanent shadowing trap. FIX: deploy/asset-refresh.sh -> refresh_asset_dir SRC DST MANIFEST [KEEP] -- install the manifest, PRUNE anything the repo cannot vouch for (INCLUDING a manifest asset the source kit no longer ships: an honest 404 beats a confident stale render), then VERIFY byte-for-byte with cmp. KEEP-LIST exists for exactly one reason: /opt/splash has TWO installers (this step = 3 served assets + version.txt; the kit's install.sh = SVGs + shutdown surface), so pruning to only what THIS step installs would delete the other installer's work mid-deploy and an A-9 skip would leave NO splash -- worse than the stale one. /opt/dashboard has one installer, no keep-list. WHY A LIBRARY FILE instead of inline in the remote heredoc: it makes the logic ACTUALLY TESTABLE. tests/deploy/test_asset_refresh.py sources the SAME function that runs on the Pi (sync_tree rsyncs it there) and drives it against temp dirs with ASSET_SUDO= -- real behaviour, not a grep of deploy-pi.sh. 7 behavioural + 4 wiring tests. The failed-write case shims the `install` BINARY to a no-op via PATH, so production code is untouched and only the system tool underneath is neutered -- worth reusing whenever a shell step's failure branch needs proving. DELIBERATE POSTURE CHANGE, PM/ATLAS PLEASE REVIEW: ABSENCE still warns-and-continues (A-9 unchanged); a FAILED WRITE now BLOCKS (non-zero, set -e aborts). Different facts -- absence is a Pi never given a UI; a failed write is a deploy that BELIEVES it shipped one and did not. The abort lands before step_restart_service, so a blocked deploy is a half-deploy; I judged a loud half-deploy better than a silent stale one, but that is the CIO's to overrule. CHECKED AND CLEAN, no action needed: the SPLASH kit does NOT have the same CSS defect (#degraded-msg/#amber-ring declare no `display`, so the UA rule applies unopposed) -- no TD filed. carousel.js reads NO element geometry anywhere (grepped getBoundingClientRect/offset*/client*), so hiding six previously-always-rendered elements cannot perturb layout math. GREEN (synchronous, in-loop): tests/ui 200 passed (8 new); tests/deploy 325 passed/1 skipped (11 new, incl. the full bash smoke test forking ~10 dry-run deploys); bash -n clean on both shell files; ruff clean on both new test files; and I ran `bash deploy/deploy-pi.sh --dry-run` and READ the two asset steps' output to confirm the wiring renders the right SRC/DST/manifest/keep-list. HOST GAPS unchanged (Sprints 64/65): make, black, mypy all absent on this Windows box -- ran ruff directly; PM please run mypy at integration time (only new Python here is test files). ARCHITECTURE DoD met in-sprint (Rule 10): specs/architecture.md F-092 section gained a 'Surface invariant: hidden means NOT RENDERED' subsection and an '/opt asset-ownership contract' subsection (manifest/keep-list table + the search-order shadowing hazard + the A-9 posture change). ON-PI GATE OWED (AC-4, undischargeable from a dev box), AND THE ORDER MATTERS: run the DEPLOY FIRST AND READ ITS OUTPUT -- the refresh now PRINTS every pruned file, and those 'pruned stale asset X' lines ARE the diagnosis of this mystery. Capture them before they scroll. Then: no-DTC dashboard load (no overlay paints, carousel clean+clickable), trigger one overlay (only that one, dismissable), wordmark reads 'ECLIPSE OBD-II'. NOTE: that wordmark is the SPLASH's #wordmark, NOT a dashboard top-bar element -- the dashboard top bar has no wordmark in this generation, which is itself corroboration that the Pi renders a retired one. If it STILL reads 'ODB2' after a deploy that shows no prune and a clean verify, the stale copy is NOT in /opt and the next suspect is the chromium kiosk profile cache (states_http already sends Cache-Control: no-store, so that would be a NEW finding -> route to Atlas). Carried debt unchanged: TD-067, TD-068.
